A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EGAgent research. All pages, including appendices, tables, figures, and equations, support comparison. The implementation appendix moves from Appendix E in v2 to Appendix F in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original EGAgent evaluations on EgoLifeQA and Video-MME (Long), plus tool ablations, oracle experiments, retrieval analyses, latency measurements, and a graph-quality audit.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds four qualitative EGAgent failure cases from EgoLifeQA.

M1.justification: The revised implementation listing specifies tool queues, completion checks after queued tools, and direct entity-graph output to memory without a separate analyzer. However, Algorithm 1 and Figure 6 retain the analyzer path, and v2 already inconsistently described one versus three tools per step. The PDFs do not resolve whether implemented inference changed or inconsistent documentation was clarified.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same EgoLifeQA coverage and Video-MME (Long) subset. The four added failure examples concern existing EgoLifeQA questions; they introduce no new dataset, population, domain, or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and appendix comparisons. Retained methods include EgoButler, Ego-R1, VideoAgent, Video-RAG, AdaVideoRAG, DrVideo, and VideoDeepResearch.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 revises the stated source of timestamps used for retrieval recall: v2 describes analyzer-selected timestamps generally, while v3 distinguishes analyzer outputs, combined transcript retrieval/relevance outputs, and formatted entity-graph SQL rows. This is a limited reported protocol correction; recomputation is not established. Sampling budgets, recall windows, and oracle settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix E and Figure 8 examine four failure cases involving identity attribution, conflicting audio and visual evidence, incomplete graph relationships, and question ambiguity. Existing tool ablations, oracle tests, retrieval analyses, and the 100-relationship audit are retained.

E5.justification: Both implementation appendices explicitly state that reported accuracies come from a single run. v3 adds no repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the TaskMaster advantage over uniformly sampled Gemini 2.5 Pro from 17.5 to 22.2 percentage points, matching the unchanged scores of 74.6 and 52.4 in Table 1 and Figure 4. Figure 8 adds four qualitative prediction outcomes. Numerical entries in Tables 1–8 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task mapping, graph definitions, Equations 1–5, and recall formula are retained. The visual-similarity expression corrects a frame symbol from x_t to v_t without changing the mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same entity-graph and agentic-reasoning contributions and performance claims. Headline accuracies remain 57.5% on EgoLifeQA and 74.1% on Video-MME (Long).

C2.justification: Appendix E adds substantive explanations of identity-grounding errors, prioritization of verbal intent over visual evidence, missing social relationships, and ambiguous preference questions. It suggests persistent persona representations, consistency checks, and targeted planning as possible remedies. These extend v2's broader upstream-perception and diarization limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix F expands and revises the LangGraph implementation example with structured plans, tool queues, dispatch nodes, and completion handling. v3 also specifies SQLite storage for visual embeddings and corrects prompt/schema descriptions. Hardware, temperatures, retry limits, graph-extraction details, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. The references match after accounting for whitespace and pagination.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections and rewrites portions of Section 3.3 and the implementation discussion. It adds acknowledgements and a failure-case appendix, renumbers the implementation appendix, and updates cross-references without broadly restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds the four-panel Figure 8 showing questions, retrieved frames, predictions, and failure explanations. It also revises several captions and adjusts table, text, and code-block placement. Existing figures and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The failure cases provide useful diagnostic evidence beyond v2's general limitations, and the corrected TaskMaster comparison improves numerical accuracy. More explicit implementation documentation also helps, although its analyzer description remains inconsistent with Algorithm 1 and Figure 6. Figure 8d additionally contains an unrelated reason about Tasha and steamed buns. These defects limit, but do not outweigh, the added diagnostic value and reporting corrections.
